text: {"claims":[{"cid":"c1","text":"A meta-regression of 16 UK studies finds no overall practically significant adverse employment effect from minimum wage increases.","cited_pids":["5f591435f1d8#0"]},{"cid":"c2","text":"There may be a genuine adverse employment effect from minimum wage increases in residential home care.","cited_pids":["5f591435f1d8#0"]},{"cid":"c3","text":"A review co-authored by Arindrajit Dube reports that most US minimum wage studies find no job losses or only small disemployment effects.","cited_pids":["f3df8a818b8c#0"]},{"cid":"c4","text":"A study of low-wage jobs finds the overall number of such jobs essentially unchanged over five years after minimum wage increases, with some reduction in tradeable sectors.","cited_pids":["e0f83db9d354#1"]},{"cid":"c5","text":"Nursing facility studies find no reduction in hours worked by lower-paid nurses after minimum wage increases.","cited_pids":["fb83e4fd4a0d#1"]},{"cid":"c6","text":"Congressional Budget Office estimates for a $15 federal minimum wage project about 1.4 million fewer jobs.","cited_pids":["6de9116294ca#3"]},{"cid":"c7","text":"Older work on youth employment reports declines of roughly 1 to 2 percent in employment per 10 percent increase in the minimum wage.","cited_pids":["ad8b67a3ca55#10"]},{"cid":"c8","text":"The weight of recent evidence favours small or no overall employment effects from raising the minimum wage.","cited_pids":[]}]}
